column1: chapter|day|location|cast|scene_1|scene_2|scene_3|exit_consequence

1|1|Meridian registration lane and market|Nil;Baker;Ama;Tobi;Collector|A repair job with a bed closes while Nil is sent between employer and registrar; the private NIL field is distinguished from a chosen name.|Bowl washing earns food and Tobi's joke; Baker supplies a specific Bazaar repair lead rather than another circular refusal.|Ama's receipt is disputed; Nil abandons the safe Bazaar route and steps between Tobi and the collection case.|The Collector must answer Nil's interruption; anonymity and the apprenticeship route can no longer be pursued unchanged.

2|1|Market arch and canal rail|Nil;Ama;Tobi;Collector;Baker;Debt Hound|Ama identifies her six confiscated units and disputed return; the Collector starts a separate final seizure while retaining her receipt.|Nil's first physical intervention fails and scrapes the right palm; they stay and bridge an exposed return channel, transferring jar6 to Ama01→07.|Ama regains her receipt, Tobi passes Baker's bun to Nil, and the Collector sees NaN; Nil draws the Hound away from the family.|The family uses the laundry stairs while Nil must take the canal service route with an injured hand.

3|1|Service stairs and Nought's shrine|Nil;cart resident;Nought;Debt Hound|The four-footed machine blocks the obvious escape; Nil cannot repeat the jar trick at an unrelated locked gate.|A resident moves a laundry cart and Nil reaches the open-hand door; Nought hides the lamp before asking questions.|Water, cloth, a chair and shared bread precede disclosure; Nought offers rest, a back exit or an explained Naming attempt.|Nil chooses to hear the Naming's risks; shelter remains available without accepting it.

4|1|Naming shrine and relay district|Nil;Nought;Ivo;Thale|Nil adopts the private designation as their chosen name; Nought writes it down independently of the terminal.|Nil chooses resonance7, keeps NaN and asks whether the choice was wrong; Nought says no and disconnects the failing query.|Physical relay alarms announce REMAINDER DETECTED; Ivo witnesses Thale setting aside dinner to trace the shrine, without access to his private thoughts.|Nought directs Nil toward Gus while the city begins an organized hunt.

5|1|Ward service yard|Nil;Nought;Vesper;Debt Hound|Nought routes Nil out and remains to answer the search; Nil survives a bounded solo stake without confusing defeat with Civic death.|Vesper intervenes before mentioning seven fen; she demonstrates one defensive decision rather than lecturing all patterns.|Nil helps secure their exit instead of fleeing alone; Vesper stays despite not being paid and gives a Bazaar route.|A reluctant partnership has a destination and an unresolved price rather than instant trust.

6|1|Bazaar and forge lane|Nil;Vesper;Gus;Maeve;Livia|The duo coordinates under pursuit; Gus repairs the decoder strap and offers three free charms, of which Nil chooses Horseshoe.|Maeve refuses to abandon a threatened forge; Nil and Vesper help preserve its tools and she negotiates travel rather than being collected as a reward.|They glimpse Livia06 behind a guarded window; Gus marks its location on a receipt while Maeve prepares a practical departure bundle.|Varro blocks the drain gate and names Nil's bounty; the window changes how the group understands the confrontation.

7|2|Drain gate and roof route|Nil;Vesper;Maeve;Varro|Varro captures the third scoring token after a completed nonterminal round; Vesper and Nil read the three-round release boundary together.|The group wins the stake, leaving Varro alive and Civic61 unchanged; Nil refuses another seizure despite learning of Livia.|Seal1 releases the local monopoly credential; Maeve gives the imperfect friend-luck charm, and a confiscation/toll receipt supplies a ferry lead; a brief dice-eyed dream asks only the chosen digit.|Mercy costs the fast ferry; the party chooses the slower Hyakki route with Varro's need unresolved.

8|3|Canal ferry to Hyakki|Nil;Vesper;Maeve;Tetsu|Tetsu checks the released toll receipt and charges a disclosed crossing fee from their travel funds.|An old Collector seam appears while he repairs a line; he declines a request for his whole history but teaches a practical knot.|Weather delays their arrival and forces a shared repair; Vesper must let Maeve lead a task she cannot bluff.|They enter Hyakki after the easy shrine-road passage has closed for the night.

9|4|Moon Pier and Night Parade|Nil;Vesper;Maeve;Hina|The party uses the parade to avoid a toll inspection; Hina names ordinary wishes Nil has never allowed themself.|A neighbour's manifestation thins when a local vow channel fails; Hina's fear interrupts her theatrical confidence.|Hina chooses to guide them to Ofuku rather than accept a court assurance she cannot verify.|Shelter and information now depend on a household relationship, not only a route through the festival.

10|4|Ofuku's shrine workshop|Nil;Maeve;Hina;Ofuku;Vesper|The elderly human keeper assigns practical restoration tasks and disagrees with Hina over what should be kept.|Maeve fixes an umbrella rib without asking and removes a familiar patch; Hina objects and Maeve restores the salvaged piece rather than defending her intent.|Ofuku's care supplies a specific shared history; a court notice offers permanence if the unregistered traveller is surrendered.|Hina must seek evidence from Enma before deciding whether the court's promise is rescue or confinement.

11|5|Enma's archive gate|Nil;Hina;Maeve;Vesper;Enma|Enma states a nonlethal access trial with an explicit cancellation; cooperation resolves the condition without injuring the keeper.|His ledger contains no page for Nil; he certifies the absence in his own book but cannot certify the absence of personhood everywhere.|Nil learns Carry through the bounded trial and accepts a witnessed counter-copy; Hina keeps it safe for the journey.|Absence becomes evidence to compare elsewhere, not a complete explanation of Nil's origin.

12|6|Foxfire approach|Nil;Hina;Ao;Aka;Tamamo|Ao values the court's protection while Aka doubts its frozen promise; their paired challenge exposes different motives.|Hina hears what permanence would preserve and what change it would prohibit; Nil refuses to make the decision for her.|The twins permit an audience under a bounded claim; Tamamo states the price openly enough for Hina to answer.|Hina's own fear, not a stolen captive, drives the palace decision.

13|6|Tamamo's palace|Nil;Hina;Vesper;Maeve;Tamamo;Ao;Aka|Tamamo shows real losses rather than a fabricated threat; Hina is tempted by stability and admits it.|The group exposes illusion channels in a declared Audit; Hina refuses to purchase recognition with Nil's freedom.|Tamamo survives; Hina claims personhood at99 and insists that restoration work continue for spirits who are still fading.|The court must negotiate reopened care channels instead of declaring belief or victory a universal cure.

14|7|Shrine road and River-bound ferry; Meridian Comptroller office interlude|Nil;Hina;Ofuku;Tamamo;Tetsu;Ivo;Thale|A witnessed road-channel agreement breaks the court monopoly and yields Seal9; Enma's counter-copy remains with Hina.|Ofuku and restoration workers disagree about priorities but begin a shared queue; Maeve assists under Hina's direction.|The toll release transfers a documented obligation to the Exchange; the party leaves with the ledger reference and a question-shaped dream, not a cage image.|Jinling has a financial reason to intervene when the party reaches Bāfā.

15|8|Bāfā harbour and pawnshop|Nil;Vesper;Maeve;Hina;Jinling;Little Lantern|Little Lantern returns a stolen charm with a purchase message; the party follows the named buyer rather than a random inn.|Jinling purchases the bounty claim but offers shelter with terms the party can inspect, refuse and leave.|Nil distinguishes protection from ownership and negotiates a guest arrangement; harbour records reveal the contested toll.|Jinling needs help comparing records while the party needs a safe way to examine the claim against them.

16|9|Exchange back rooms and dock cooperative|Nil;Jinling;Vesper;dock witnesses|Tea and guarded humour precede a look at Jinling's private debt relief; Vesper recognizes a mark and conceals its personal significance.|Nil treats an apparent match as conclusive and authorizes use of their comparison despite an unstated uncertainty.|An innocent dock cooperative's reserve is frozen; workers confront Nil and Jinling instead of applauding cleverness.|The investigation cannot proceed honestly until Nil corrects their claim and helps restore the cooperative's access.

17|10|Harbour records and Hall approach|Nil;Jinling;Bai Si;dock witnesses|Nil withdraws the false certainty publicly; Jinling releases the disputed freeze from a documented review route without raiding deposits.|Independent discrepancies remain after that correction; Bai Si meets the party carrying four lanterns and asks who will preserve contradictory testimony.|A knot used by Wen the ferry-rope maker identifies a life behind the old missing fraction; Nil agrees to compare living and death records independently.|The dead-count inquiry has a named human stake and a reason for the descent.

18|11|Naihe crossing and Ten Courts|Nil;Bai Si;Jinling;Ox-Head;Horse-Face;witness|The paired wardens define an objective that requires simultaneous cooperation, then bow when it is fulfilled.|A preserved witness account of Wen conflicts with the rounded official entry; Bai Si records both instead of discarding the testimony.|An independently preserved dead count shows the same direction of loss as corrected living records, not yet its destination.|Judge Cui can test whether a bounded correction preserves its original evidence.

19|11|Judge Cui's record hall|Nil;Bai Si;Jinling;Judge Cui|The Brush trial requires a counter-copy, a named source and an amendable entry; no blank cheque to rewrite lives is offered.|Nil performs a limited correction and learns Rewrite; the dead-count extract is witnessed and copied before return.|Bai Si chooses to travel with the party because their method permits uncertainty and correction, not because his grief is solved.|The harbour must now answer independently verified evidence it cannot dismiss as a private ledger mistake.

20|12|Exchange archive and Jin Chan's office|Nil;Jinling;Vesper;Bai Si;Jin Chan|Jinling protects true accounts before burning enforcement copies; her confrontation identifies the hidden payers of protected-route allocations.|The father's Audit stake ends without killing him; workers and depositors contest whether his daughter should simply inherit control.|Vesper admits the rigged hand and Mara Vale's harm without demanding reassurance; an archive correction bears Ivo's initials.|The party has evidence of a system, a companion's withheld culpability and a release order that still has not helped Livia.

21|13|Bāfā public hearing and departure; Meridian Comptroller office interlude|Nil;Jinling;workers;depositors;Nought by letter;Ivo by record;Ivo;Thale|A provisional reserve board includes workers and depositors; relief below eight fen is funded from distributable owner surplus, not wages or deposits.|Seal8 breaks the monopoly; Jinling retains a protected true-account copy while Bai Si retains the dead-count extract; Ivo's dated correction transmits the rejected decentralization proposal and Livia's withheld order.|Nought's dated reply explains Open Hand as shelter rather than a command; the party sends its new observatory lead back through the established courier route, without inventing an instant acknowledgment.|The records require independent measurement; the party leaves a contested functioning board and an active correspondence route behind.

22|14|Road to Śūnyapura and observatory guest room|Nil;Shunya;Vidya Rao;Meera;Jinling|Travel consumes paid provisions and time; an instrument crew's missing wages complicate an apparently hospitable scholarly invitation.|Shunya offers chai and a hypothesis, then Nil sets limits before anyone touches the decoder.|Meera brings a named request for her brother's record; Jinling challenges Shunya over releasing financial data.|An inquiry becomes a negotiated collaboration with personal and institutional costs.

23|15|Stepwell retrieval route|Nil;Meera;Shunya;Maeve;Bai Si|Meera establishes ropes, lamps, depth and a return boundary; the descent cannot rely on resurrection or a universal decoder trick.|The recovered record represents a lost life, not the body; Shunya's equal-quantity model fails to preserve a timed event in a small inert test using nonpersonal calibration pulses.|Nil returns the private record to Meera and obtains permission for a limited comparison, preserving the failed result.|Quantities alone are insufficient; timing and the meaning of regional claims must be compared.

24|16|Observatory and Chitragupta's hall|Nil;Shunya;Vidya Rao;Chitragupta|Shunya states scope, risks, stopping conditions and separate publication rights; Nil agrees to examination, not public ownership.|The keeper's nonlethal record trial supplies another independent source with its own meaning rather than an identical missing coin.|New data requires a fresh question and renewed consent; Shunya preserves the rejected model instead of quietly replacing it.|The investigators have enough independent signatures to test an origin hypothesis without narrating it as fact yet.

25|17|Observatory comparison room|Nil;Shunya;Bai Si;Jinling;Vesper|Witness copies align fractional signatures across living, dead and deed records; each source's limits remain visible.|Nil catches the urge to offer the answer others want and asks whether the evidence is sufficient; Shunya distinguishes what it proves from what it cannot explain.|Independent checks converge on accumulation into a self-aware account; the chapter ends on Nil asking for the plain conclusion.|The next chapter must answer clearly rather than prolong mystery through evasive terminology.

26|18|Observatory quiet room and courtyard|Nil;Shunya;Bai Si;Maeve;Vesper|Shunya states that discarded fractions became Nil; there is no proof here of the physical captive source or a divine lineage.|Companions react imperfectly; Nil refuses further testing for the afternoon, and Shunya respects it without withdrawing shelter.|Bai Si writes Wen's disputed name into his continuing record; Nil chooses to stop suppressor interference rather than accept a public demonstration of their body; that evening they voluntarily learn Place Value on an inert instrument, not through renewed personal examination.|Identity knowledge changes agency and boundaries; the engine mission follows Nil's own decision.

27|19|Plateau eclipse-engine works|Nil;Shunya;Vidya Rao;surveyors;companions|The party documents operator stamps on invented bolted machines, separating the surveyors' acts from revered celestial figures.|They disable linked suppressors through ordinary bounded Audits and maintenance access; the natural eclipse passes without killing a deity.|Seal0 releases the control monopoly; Vidya records brightness varies, while Shunya offers restricted co-authorship and preserves the equation's unresolved scaling limit.|The observatory can publish measurements; Thale learns suppression has failed through the resulting report.

28|20|Observatory dispatch room and Kroton road|Nil;Shunya;Jinling;Vidya Rao;courier|The protected equation copy includes the failed timing test, a corrected bounded model and an explicit warning against mass deployment.|A public acceleration order names the Sieve schedule; Shunya issues independently signed observation copies, while Ivo's earlier proposal identifies a possible decentralized institution.|The party uses a paid caravan route, sends councils a request to consider a bounded transition, and chooses Kroton because children face a dated threat.|Travel follows a specific imminent policy rather than a new unlocked biome; no regional mandate is assumed merely because a letter was sent.

29|21|Kroton arrival terraces|Nil;Prima;Synod guards;Niko|Prima escorts the party as prisoners under an exclusion order she believes temporary; she shows real shelter work alongside doctrinal rank.|A goat-herd's mishap exposes the unsafe terrace edge without making endangered residents a joke.|Nil asks about appeal and Prima supplies a route that excludes people she has previously turned away.|The prisoners must pass through the undercity before the schedule can be challenged.

30|22|Kallisto's undercity workshops|Nil;Prima;Kallisto;workers;Maeve|Workers demonstrate the supports they maintain beneath the official city; Kallisto names a family Prima denied passage.|Prima cannot repair the injury by citing good intentions; Maeve recognizes parts of the old machine in ordinary workshop repairs.|A signed school-transfer order reveals that children will be moved across a failing Sieve section before an appeal can reach the temple.|Prima must choose between the command she carries and people whose danger she can now verify.

31|23|School evacuation and Sieve span|Nil;Prima;Kallisto;children;workers|Prima orders a halt and is refused; she opens her shield to support the trapped children, visibly breaking her office's command.|A small consenting rescue team uses the corrected translation model on named stakes; it succeeds locally while the monopoly prevents wider scaling.|Prima accepts workers' direction and surrenders her access logs for evidence rather than asking for immediate forgiveness.|The rescue proves a limited alternative and exposes both the remaining lock and Prima's earlier complicity.

32|24|Moirai's route and measured cave|Nil;Prima;Clotho;Lachesis;Atropos;companions|The sequence trial asks coordinated action rather than injury to a keeper.|Lachesis measures relationships with permission; Prima and Nil work through disagreement instead of gaining a proof from numerical compatibility alone.|Atropos offers an expendable ribbon as the declared sacrifice; protected proofs are not consumed and the thread is witnessed for later release.|The group learns Factor and returns with a trial record, not an unlimited power over anyone's life.

33|24|Undercity archive workshop|Nil;Maeve;Bai Si;Kallisto;Prima|Maeve identifies a first-generation gear through an independently dated repair log, showing the institution predates Thale.|Bai Si smiles at a River-born worker's inherited account of Wen's ropework rather than a perfect total; Prima helps prepare testimony without directing the residents.|The gear's financing reference connects old machinery to the House's later maintenance network; Vesper agrees to disclose the risk before departure.|The temple confrontation now has evidence, a repair objective and witnesses who will still govern after the party leaves.

34|25|Archon's access court|Nil;Prima;Archon;Kallisto;companions|Residents present access logs and the failed school order; the Archon refuses review while claiming the system protects the city.|The bounded Audit removes declared faces; the party adapts through legal remaining options rather than inventing a new ability.|Defeat damages the physical Sieve support; Prima's teacher falls beyond the safe edge before the outcome can become a victory speech.|Saving a defeated opponent becomes a costly action rather than automatic institutional restoration.

35|26|Sieve edge and reopening hearing|Nil;Prima;Maeve;Archon;Kallisto;Vesper|Prima catches the Archon and others share the load; Civic17 remains distinct from his exhausted stake, and custody passes to witnesses.|Lachesis's witnessed thread is released to Prima, Seal2 breaks the monopoly and Maeve forges the first-gear horseshoe only after asking what Nil needs.|Residents control the reopened routes; Vesper gives the fuller Mara history and the party consents to follow the financing trail through a paid westbound passage.|The party leaves copies and testimony, carries two more proofs and accepts a journey whose personal danger Vesper has finally named.

36|27|Crossroads road and midnight junction|Nil;Vesper;Stranger;companions|Caravan travel and a shelter letter place the group outside Lucky Strike before the local loop boundary.|The Stranger declares the terms of a fair trial and teaches a bounded Deal with an explicit refusal option.|Vesper identifies the casino and former associates instead of pretending to be an uninvolved guide.|The group knowingly enters a repeating jurisdiction with a skill and an articulated risk.

37|28 night|Lucky Strike local iteration1597|Nil;Fibi;Vesper;House staff|The party enters during the1597th iteration; Fibi predicts a routine but cannot finish Nil's new reply.|She tests whether their memories and records differ from her prior visitors; Nil's unregistered account anchors the arriving party after entry.|Fibi chooses to show the motel at three and confides her wish to train as a road surveyor.|The investigation proceeds by her permission rather than treating her as a puzzle object to extract.

38|28 night|Motel and railway inside local iteration1597|Nil;Fibi;Penny;Vance|At three, Fibi reconstructs previous repeated events and distinguishes memory from current observation.|Penny's authorized nonspendable penny tokens and Vance's retained case markers corroborate1596 completed loops; they are not farmable currency.|The group observes the protection mechanism's current debit and identifies Fibi's heart stopping as the reset condition, without causing another death to prove it.|They have a testable mechanism and a reason to seek the signed maintenance clause before dawn.

39|28 night|House contract office|Nil;Fibi;House;Vance;Jinling|The recovered maintenance clause identifies source, debit and cancellation; protection itself drains Fibi at dawn.|Fibi consents to ending it after hearing what safety it actually supplied; the House refuses to release its control claim.|Vesper tries to make the conversation about her own guilt; Fibi asks her to leave, and she does.|Fibi's decision is settled but execution requires a changed House signature and protected original terms.

40|28 before dawn|Mutual-aid office and honest table|Nil;Vesper;Fibi;Mara;Vance;House|Mara refuses a reunion on Vesper's terms through her own mutual-aid office; Vesper supplies a witnessed statement and directs restitution to the family's chosen fund.|Vesper deals Fibi a game with open rules and accepts a fair loss; Fibi is not required to forgive or console her.|The table exposes the House's rewind limits under the recovered terms; the group begins a bounded confrontation to compel release of its unlawful control claim.|The victory must yield a signature and a lawful cancellation, not simply damage that cures Fibi.

41|29 dawn|Lucky Strike cancellation table|Nil;Fibi;House;Vance;companions|The House's bounded stake ends and it relinquishes the claim with a witnessed signature; Fibi separately confirms consent.|The cancellation closes the maintenance drain; Fibi survives the first new dawn with fatigue and uncertain plans, and keeps control of her recollections.|Seal7 releases the monopoly; Fibi keeps the Black Book page and Vesper the marked deck, with witness copies; staff begin wage and property proceedings.|The required six Seals exist, but returning safely requires Livia's unresolved transfer and regional replies.

42|30|Crossroads courier station and return convoy|Nil;Fibi;Vesper;Varro;Livia by letter;Gus;Nought|Gus's courier delivers Livia's symptom log and consent to medical transfer using the dated River order; Nought confirms ordinary care and separately funded route protection.|Varro removes the mask and chooses restitution as a guest; no Civic units are created as payment for his recruitment.|Council replies and reserve schedules arrive through established carriers; a paid convoy carries the group home over the following three days.|The party carries evidence and limited mandates, not sovereign power; Fibi joins the road by her own choice.

43|33|Meridian outer camp|Nil;all eight core companions;Varro;regional delegates|The camp reviews each protected proof, its owner, counter-copy, permitted use and the two earlier translation tests.|Delegates ratify limited revocable mandates and named emergency pools after dissent is recorded; Nil hears that injury and failure remain possible.|Nil chooses the bounded attempt, preserves a withdrawal condition and declines any claim to inherit government.|All final prerequisites are now available before the ritual rather than conjured by a climax speech.

44|34|Basilica Upper Gate and service passage|Nil;companions;Ivo;guards|Recalled exterior guards do not open the ritual gate; six office credentials and chosen resonance7 occupy seven distinct keyed sockets.|The opened gate still leads to a separate internal barrier; Ivo uses the route seeded by his earlier copies and accepts witnessed responsibility for his part.|The group follows original account routes through archive corridors, preserving records rather than destroying every trace of the institution.|They reach the heart through acquired access and a person's deliberate defection, not teleportation or a prophecy.

45|34|Basilica heart|Nil;companions;Hap;Ivo|The party first sees the physical closed brass fist and starving Hap; the reader is not told it was visible in earlier dreams.|Original records connect the registered fractions to captive possibility, completing the origin's second stage without declaring Nil a deity or property.|Hap can now speak directly; Nil asks about people injured by free chance and refuses a demand that freedom mean returning to unaccountable rule.|The final choice must solve coercive allocation without pretending a liberated god is automatically just.

46|34|Basilica operator archive|Nil;Thale;Ivo;Jinling;Shunya|Independent original dates distinguish TR702 construction, TR985 inheritance and TR999 discovery; the rejected decentralization proposal matches Ivo's earlier copy.|Thale admits the protected-route benefits and hidden costs and explains why he rejected a power-sharing alternative.|Nil and the witnesses name their limited mandate and continuity pools; disagreement concerns authority and risk after the arithmetic is understood.|Thale chooses Fixed Fate despite a documented alternative, making the confrontation an informed coercive act.

47|34|Even Hand control floor|Nil;Thale;companions|The bounded confrontation tests declared channels while crews preserve essential coverage; no ordinary strike generates new Civic luck.|Compression slows available options toward stillness; the party must protect the record routes and people maintaining them.|Nil appears isolated when the shared channel closes, but their earlier refusal to treat companions as expendable leaves independent routes intact.|The next response must come from those distinct prior commitments rather than an unseeded collective power.

48|34|Control floor and witness station|Nil;Thale;all eight core companions;Ivo|Companions answer through specific previously established routes, tools and authorized records; none is reduced to a number in a friendship attack.|Thale's stake ends without automatic Civic settlement; he yields executive control and preserves the operator record under witness custody.|Nil reconfirms the attempt with each contributor and the emergency-pool stewards; the equation cannot substitute for their permission.|The mechanism can now be enacted as a bounded institutional transition, not merely a boss reward.

49|35–36;one year later|Meridian workshops and regional epilogues|Nil;companions;regional councils;Livia;Varro;Hap;Thale|Eight protected records support the witnessed translation; the fist opens, rounding monopoly ends and reserves bridge the switch without claiming infinite luck.|Nil receives separate Civic07 and resonance7, chooses the apprenticeship rather than office; councils begin appeals while Thale faces proceedings, not a sentimental pardon.|Linked regional aftermaths show work, unresolved disagreements and unrepaired loss; a clearly marked one-year jump gives Hina her100th birthday and Fibi another chosen departure.|The central conflict closes while ordinary repair continues; no sequel is required to explain Nil's personhood or the new institutions' limits.
